title: Buying Off-Plan: To Live In or to Flip?
seoTitle: Buying Off-Plan to Live In or to Flip?
description: There are two reasons to buy off-plan: to live in the home or to profit from it. Each one changes how you choose the unit and which risks matter.
answer: If you buy off-plan to live in, the unit must fit your life and you accept waiting for completion. If you buy to profit, you choose a unit within budget with strong resale potential and plan to assign the contract before completion. Both carry delay risk.
body:
People buy off-plan property for one of two reasons. Knowing which one is yours changes everything about how you choose.

## Reason one: you want to live there

You are buying a brand-new home before it is built, at the lowest price it will ever have. The trade-off is time: you wait until the developer finishes the building.

When you buy to live in, the unit has to fit you. Layout, light, view, the size of each room, the floor, the neighbourhood. You will spend years in it, so the details matter more than the resale curve.

## Reason two: you want to make money

You buy the contract early, usually in the presale phase, and **assign** it to someone else later, often when the building is close to completion, at a higher price. You never live there and you may never even own it.

Here you evaluate the unit differently. First, it must fit your budget, including all the deposits. Second, it must be the kind of unit that will be in demand when the building is finished: the right size, the right price bracket, the layout most end buyers want.

## The risks are the same in both cases

- **Delays.** Projects get delayed by material shortages, permits, or problems found during construction.
- **Delivery.** The finished building may differ from what was promised.
- **Market.** Prices can move against you before completion.

You reduce these risks the same way in both cases: by doing your due diligence on the developer, the project and the unit before you sign.
takeaways: Decide first whether you are buying to live in or to profit.
A home must fit your life; an investment must fit your budget and future demand.
Investors usually profit by assigning the contract before completion.
Delays and market changes are risks in both cases, and due diligence reduces them.
faq: Is it better to buy off-plan to live in or to invest?
Neither is better in general. It depends on your goal, your budget and how long you can wait. Just be clear which one you are doing before choosing a unit.
What kind of unit is best for flipping an off-plan contract?
Usually the units with the widest demand at completion, such as well-priced one and two bedrooms with good layouts, rather than the most unusual or expensive units.
How long will I wait to move in?
Typically two to three years from launch, but delays happen, so check the developer's history of delivering on time.
